patches.name: Watch without signing in
patches.description: Opens Twitch without an account instead of stopping at the Log In / Sign Up screen, using Twitch's own signed-out mode. Streams, videos and chat can be watched; following, chatting and other account actions still ask you to sign in. Signed-in use is unchanged.

patches.name: Avoid stitched ads
patches.description: While Twitch's server stitches an ad break into a live stream, plays the stream instead from a picture-by-picture session, the kind Twitch itself shows during breaks, which gets no ads: at 360p at most, with sound, then back to the stream's own session and quality when the break is over. The player doesn't reload. The playback token for that session is requested without your account. If a break runs past 4 minutes or the stream's own playlist stops answering, the stream comes back on a new session instead; when your own token has under a minute left, that session's token is also requested without your account, and the rest of the stream plays as a signed-out viewer's (how that affects subscriber ad exemption, minutes watched and Drops is untested). When no picture-by-picture session can be had, the break plays, and Mute stitched ads still mutes and covers it. Native and React Native players; streams started while it's off are left alone, and turning it off during a break lets that break finish on picture-by-picture first. Does nothing for streams loaded through Playlist proxy.

patches.name: Block client ads
patches.description: Declines ads handled by Twitch's native client ad eligibility check using its existing not eligible result. Does not remove ads stitched into streams by the server or guarantee ad-free playback.

patches.name: Block display ads
patches.description: Blocks the ad requests that Block client ads doesn't cover: stream display ads (squeezeback and lower third), audio ads, multi-format ad pods, the Following headliner, feed display and video ads and brand surveys, in both the native and React Native parts of the app. Each request gets the failure or no-ad answer Twitch already handles. Sponsorship and paid-promotion labels are kept. Ads stitched into the stream by the server still play.

patches.name: Mute stitched ads
patches.description: While an ad break that Twitch's server stitched into a stream plays, mutes the player and covers the video with black, then restores both when the stream returns. Works in the native and React Native players. The ad still plays and the break isn't shorter.

patches.name: Disable analytics
patches.description: Stops Twitch's native and React Native Spade event uploads, denies local analytics SDK consent, enables Branch's limited tracking mode, blocks Crashlytics uploads, Nielsen audience pings and Sprig surveys, and prevents Sentry initialization. Watch progress, viewing statistics and rewards may stop updating. Restart Twitch after changing this setting. Playback requests still run.

patches.name: Third-party badges
patches.description: Adds switches that show FrankerFaceZ, Chatterino and 7TV badges and pronouns.alejo.io pronouns next to chatters' names in native and React Native chat. Each switch is off until turned on in Lurk settings. The FrankerFaceZ and Chatterino switches download that service's public list of all badge holders (api.frankerfacez.com, api.chatterino.com) about once an hour and check it on the phone, then load each badge's image from the https address the list names (FrankerFaceZ: cdn.frankerfacez.com; Chatterino: currently fourtf.com, but any host its list gives). The 7TV switch keeps a connection to 7TV's event service (events.7tv.io) while a channel's chat is open, which tells 7TV the channel, as the 7TV emotes switch does, and nothing about you or the chatters you see; 7TV sends the badges of that channel's chatters and their images come from cdn.7tv.app. The pronouns switch sends the username of each chatter whose message you see to pronouns.alejo.io.

patches.name: Anonymous chat
patches.description: Adds a switch that reads chat as an anonymous guest, the way Twitch does when signed out, while the rest of the app stays signed in, so you aren't listed among a channel's chatters. Sending chat messages is disabled while it's on. Off by default; applies after a restart.

patches.name: Auto-claim channel points
patches.description: Adds a switch that claims the channel points bonus for your account as soon as its chest appears in a channel's chat, with the same request as tapping the chest. Each bonus is claimed once. Needs a signed-in account. Checked against Twitch's code and with a stand-in for the claim service, not yet with a real account. The claim leaves out the chat mode a tap sends, which Twitch only adds to its analytics event. Starts off. Turn it on in Lurk settings > Chat.

patches.name: Auto-claim Drops
patches.description: Adds a switch that claims a Drop for your account as soon as Twitch's drops notification in a channel shows it as claimable, by pressing that notification's Claim button for you: the same claim request and the same "claim" analytics event a tap sends (Disable analytics blocks the event). Each drop is claimed once per app start. Needs a signed-in account and the notification, which shows while you watch a channel with Drops; drops earned elsewhere stay in your inventory. Checked against Twitch's code on Android's runtime, not yet with a real account. Starts off. Turn it on in Lurk settings > Chat.

patches.name: Chat appearance
patches.description: Adds chat look settings: text, emote and badge size, message spacing, alternating row backgrounds, plain /me messages, and the width and background opacity of the landscape chat panel. Each keeps Twitch's look until changed in Lurk settings. Native live chat, chat history and VOD chat replay; React Native chat gets the text size, row backgrounds, /me style and landscape panel only.

patches.name: Chat keywords
patches.description: Highlights chat messages that mention you or contain your highlight words with a tinted background, optionally with a vibration, and hides messages with blocked words or from blocked users. Mentions are on by default; the word and user lists start empty and are set in Lurk settings. Native and React Native live chat and history, plus native VOD chat replay.

patches.name: Chat timestamps
patches.description: Shows the time each live chat message was sent in front of it, the way Twitch already shows it on chat history, in 24-hour or 12-hour format. Whispers are unchanged.

patches.name: Compact chat
patches.description: Adds switches that leave chatters' badges out of native chat lines (Twitch's and third-party ones) and show emotes as their text, so no emote images load. Native live chat, chat history and VOD chat replay; React Native chat is unchanged. Starts off. Turn it on in Lurk settings > Chat.

patches.name: Highlight first-time chatters
patches.description: Tints a chatter's first message in a channel in native live chat, using the first-msg tag Twitch's chat server puts on it. Chat history, VOD replay and React Native chat carry no such tag. Starts off. Turn it on in Lurk settings > Chat.

patches.name: Emote and badge info
patches.description: Adds a switch that shows a small sheet when you tap an emote or a badge in native chat, chat history or VOD chat replay: the image larger, its name, where it comes from (Twitch, 7TV, BetterTTV, FrankerFaceZ, Chatterino; channel or global; who made it, when the service's list says) and a Copy name button. Signed in, Twitch emotes keep Twitch's own emote card; usernames and long presses keep what Twitch does. Native chat only; React Native chat is unchanged. Starts off. Turn it on in Lurk settings > Chat.

patches.name: Show deleted messages
patches.description: Keeps the text of chat messages that moderators delete, or remove with a timeout or ban, struck through and dimmed instead of Twitch's "message deleted" placeholder. A second switch keeps the messages when a moderator clears the whole chat.

patches.name: Clip download
patches.description: Adds "Download clip" to the menu (⋮) of a clip in Twitch's clips feed, where clip links open. It asks gql.twitch.tv for the clip's video addresses and signed access token with the app's Client-ID only (no account), and Android's download manager saves the best quality as an MP4 in Downloads/Twitch. Starts off. Turn it on in Lurk settings > Playback.

patches.name: Block cookie notice
patches.description: Hides Twitch's automatic cookie consent notice without accepting it or changing saved vendor consent. Manual consent settings stay available. Use Disable analytics to block tracking.

patches.name: Third-party emotes
patches.description: Adds switches that show 7TV, BetterTTV and FrankerFaceZ emotes in chat, Twitch's chat history and VOD chat replay. When on, each sends the ID of the channel you watch to that service (7tv.io, api.betterttv.net, api.frankerfacez.com) for its emote lists and loads the emote images from its CDN. "Emotes in the picker" also lists them in the emote picker, one section per service, and in autocomplete after ':', from the same lists; that part was checked with Twitch's own picker and autocomplete code on Android's runtime, not in the app, which needs an account to open the picker. Starts off. Turn it on in Lurk settings > Chat.

patches.name: Lurk icon
patches.description: Replaces Twitch's launcher icon with Lurk artwork, including Android's themed icon.

patches.name: Force ExoPlayer
patches.description: Adds a switch that plays live channels and videos with the ExoPlayer backend Twitch still ships instead of Amazon IVS. Off until turned on in Lurk settings. Clips, encrypted streams and React Native players stay on IVS. Lurk patches that hook IVS, such as Normal latency, Mute stitched ads and Show video stats, don't act on ExoPlayer.

patches.name: Navigation bar position
patches.description: Adds a choice that moves Twitch's bottom navigation bar to the top of the screen and/or hides its labels, leaving only the icons. Twitch's own layout stays until another choice is made in Lurk settings.

patches.name: Tablet layout
patches.description: Adds a switch that makes Twitch treat the phone as a tablet: Home and the player rotate, the player shows chat beside the video in landscape, and a navigation rail on the left replaces the bottom bar in landscape (and in portrait too with a second switch). Off until turned on in Lurk settings; applies after a restart.

patches.name: Clean share links
patches.description: Removes known Twitch attribution and campaign parameters from shared links and copied share text. Keeps timestamps, clip IDs, unknown parameters and fragments. Covers native and React Native sharing.

patches.name: Default startup tab
patches.description: Adds a choice of the screen Twitch opens on instead of Home: Browse, Following or Activity. Links and notifications still open what they point to.

patches.name: Fix notifications
patches.description: Lets the patched app register for push notifications. Firebase only accepts Twitch's original package name and signing certificate, and refuses the re-signed app, so its registration requests send the original ones, which are what unpatched Twitch sends. Registration was checked; delivering a notification needs an account and wasn't. On by default; the switch is in Lurk settings > Interface and applies after a restart.

patches.name: Chat overlay
patches.description: Adds a switch that scrolls live chat messages right to left across the top of the video in landscape (danmaku), as plain white text with the sender's name. Off until turned on in Lurk settings, with choices for speed and number of lines. Native live channels only: not React Native chat, VODs or chat replay. The overlay never takes touches.

patches.name: Remove tracking permissions
patches.description: Removes advertising ID and Google Play install-referrer permissions. Other identifiers and analytics require separate controls.

patches.name: Background audio
patches.description: Keeps streams and videos playing as audio when you leave the app, using Twitch's own "Continue Playing Audio in the Background" with its audio-only stream and media notification. Changes only the default, Never in Twitch: a choice made in Twitch's settings still wins.

patches.name: Disable autoplay
patches.description: Stops the next recommended video and React Native feed clip from playing automatically, and defaults feed previews to Never. Manual Play and saved feed preview choices keep working.

patches.name: Fill screen
patches.description: Zooms streams and videos to fill the screen in landscape, the strip beside the camera cutout included, cropping their top and bottom instead of showing black bars at the sides, on phones taller than 16:9. The player's buttons and the stream's details stay clear of the cutout. Vertical videos, the player next to the chat and picture-in-picture keep their bars. Works in the native theatre and in the React Native one Twitch can use while Use native player is off. Starts off. Turn it on in Lurk settings > Playback.

patches.name: Force landscape
patches.description: Turns the screen to landscape when a live stream or video opens in Twitch's native theatre, and back to the orientation the app had when the theatre closes. Twitch's rotate button still switches to portrait. Home's feed previews don't rotate. Starts off. Turn it on in Lurk settings > Playback.

patches.name: Latency badge
patches.description: Shows how far a live stream plays behind the broadcast on Twitch's native player in the theatre, read from the player itself once a second (the latency the stats panel reports). Tapping it reloads the stream through Twitch's own Retry, a new access token and playlist that start at the live edge: the native player has no seek to live. Feed previews, videos and clips show nothing. Starts off. Turn it on in Lurk settings > Playback.

patches.name: Normal latency
patches.description: Adds a setting that turns off the player's low-latency mode for live streams: a few seconds more delay to the broadcaster, for fewer rebuffers on a weak connection. Off until turned on in Lurk settings.

patches.name: Player gestures
patches.description: Sets the skip interval of the video (VOD) rewind and forward buttons and the media notification, and adds brightness (left) and volume (right) swipes on the video in landscape. Twitch's -10/+30 seconds stay until you choose another interval in Lurk settings; swipes start off.

patches.name: Refresh stream
patches.description: Long-press the player's settings gear, or the middle of the video, to reload a stuck stream through Twitch's own Retry: a new access token and playlist for live streams, the same position for videos. Covers Twitch's native players.

patches.name: Sleep timer
patches.description: Pauses playback a chosen time after it last started or resumed, through Twitch's own pause for native, portal and React Native players, and says so in a short notice. Choose the time in Lurk settings or in the player's settings sheet (the gear), which gets a Sleep timer row under Background audio; it is off until then.

patches.name: Fix stuck start screen
patches.description: Opens Twitch when its start screen is still waiting after 5 seconds. Twitch waits for Branch's link lookup before it routes, and when that never answers, it stays on a blank start screen until it's closed, unpatched Twitch included. On by default; the switch is in Lurk settings > Interface.

patches.name: Use native player
patches.description: Always opens live channels in Twitch's native player, never the React Native "Ultralight" player a server experiment can switch some users to. Most Lurk playback, chat and ad patches hook the native player.

patches.name: AMOLED black
patches.description: Turns the dark theme's greys black on screens drawn with Android views: the window and navigation bar, Home, Browse and channel pages, the theatre and chat, whose backgrounds are repainted after each layout. Screens Twitch draws with Compose (parts of settings, the emote picker and some sheets) and pop-up sheets keep their dark grey. Only in Twitch's dark mode. Applies after a restart. Starts off. Turn it on in Lurk settings > Interface.

patches.name: VOD chapters
patches.description: Adds a Chapters button to the native video (VOD) player that lists the stream's game and category changes and jumps to one through Twitch's own seek. The list comes from Twitch's public data: one request to gql.twitch.tv per video the native player loads, feed previews included, with the app's client ID and without your account. On by default; the switch is in Lurk settings > Playback.
